races.title: State Senate, District 34
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Avelino Valencia
cands.bio: Democrat from Anaheim. Assemblymember for District 68 since December 2022 and Anaheim City Council member for District 4 from 2020 to 2022. Earlier worked as a legislative staffer for Assemblymember Tom Daly. Holds a political science degree from San José State and an MPA from Johns Hopkins.

endorsements.text: Endorsed in the 2026 State Senate race by the Democratic Party of California, the California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO), the California Teachers Association, the National Union of Healthcare Workers, Equality California, and Planned Parenthood of Orange and San Bernardino Counties' Community Action Fund.

cands.gaps: We found no stated positions or documented actions from Valencia on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land purchases, growth and land protection, immigration and H-1B, police and public order, guns, abortion, or school choice. Ballotpedia's list of sponsored bills was empty in the page we read, so we could not cite specific legislation he wrote. He did not complete Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey in 2020, 2022, 2024 or 2026. We found no reported controversies. We found no foreign-government ties. His birthplace comes from Wikipedia alone, and neither page describes his childhood directly.

local.label: Roots 100: Wikipedia says he was born in Anaheim, and Ballotpedia says he graduated from Katella High School, attended Fullerton College, and lives in Anaheim, with local office held since 2020.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assemblymember since December 2022, Anaheim City Council member 2020–2022, and legislative staffer for Assemblymember Tom Daly (Wikipedia: 2016–2022; Ballotpedia: chief deputy and field representative). Holds an MPA in government and policy from Johns Hopkins.
qual.why: He has served in two elected offices, including the state Assembly, and spent years in legislative staff work, which matches the law-and-budget job. His committee chair role was not counted toward the score.
qual.label: He has served in two elected offices, including the state Assembly, and spent years in legislative staff work, which matches the law-and-budget job. His committee chair role was not counted toward the score.

cands.name: Rhonda Shader
cands.bio: Insurance agency owner and life and health coach in Placentia, California. First elected to the Placentia City Council in 2016, she served two terms as Mayor. Ran for State Senate District 34 as a Republican in 2022 and 2026.

endorsements.text: Listed on Ballotpedia as endorsed by the Republican Party of California and Reform California.

In her Ballotpedia survey she lists endorsements from Orange County Sheriff Don Barnes, the Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association, the Lincoln Club of Orange County, the GOP Union Caucus, California Young Republicans and California College Republicans.

cands.gaps: We could not find where she grew up or when she came to California; the pages give only her birthplace and high school. We found no documented stances on data centers, development or growth limits, foreign or institutional buyers of homes and land, immigration or H-1B, guns, or abortion. We found no statement from her on teacher pay or on refusing certain kinds of donations. Her claims about saving Placentia $28 million through its own fire department and about a 5,000-job infrastructure district come from her campaign and survey and were not independently confirmed. Her campaign Issues page was cut off partway, so some of its content was not read.

local.label: Roots 90: Ballotpedia says she was born in Whittier, CA and graduated from Buena Park High School, and she has held Placentia city office since 2016, but no page states where she grew up.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: She was elected to the Placentia City Council in 2016 and served two terms as Mayor. She owns a local insurance agency and a coaching practice, has a background in banking and risk management, and holds a paralegal degree and a management bachelor's degree.
qual.why: Local elected office with budget responsibilities plus business ownership places her in the middle band. She has no state legislative service. Her claims about city finances and the fire department come from her own campaign materials.
qual.label: Local elected office with budget responsibilities plus business ownership places her in the middle band. She has no state legislative service. Her claims about city finances and the fire department come from her own campaign materials.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: Says she will defend Proposition 13 property tax limits so families and seniors can stay in their homes, and will fight to cut taxes. She did not call for eliminating homestead property taxes.

back-police-order.evidence: Says she will fully fund and staff local law enforcement, oppose efforts to defund police, and repeal the most damaging provisions of Prop 47. She also wants Prop 36 funded.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Says she will support policies that let education funding follow the student, including charter schools. Her 2026 survey lists school choice for parents among her passions. She does not mention teacher pay in these pages.

prio.label: Matches 3 of 3 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 3 only promised
